questions.question: A template task changes a drifted file and notifies a restart handler. What should a second run report when nobody changes the host between runs?
options: The template changes again and the handler restarts again
The template is ok and the handler does not run
The host becomes unreachable because the file already exists
The task must be skipped with a when condition
questions.explanation: A convergent template task compares the desired content and metadata with the target. When they match, it reports ok, so the handler receives no new notification.

questions.question: Why does adding changed_when: false to an unconditional shell command not make the command idempotent?
options: It changes only Ansible's result classification, not the command's actual side effect
It forces the command to run twice
It disables SSH host-key verification
It converts the command into a template module
questions.explanation: changed_when controls reporting. The external command still runs and can still repeat writes, restarts, or API calls.

questions.question: What hosts can the pattern webservers:&production:!canary select?
options: Every production host whether or not it is a web server
Every web server plus every canary
Hosts that are in both webservers and production, excluding canary members
Any host whose name contains the word production
questions.explanation: The intersection operators require membership in webservers and production, while !canary removes hosts in the canary group. Patterns operate on inventory membership.

questions.question: A play uses serial: 3 and max_fail_percentage: 33. One host fails in the current three-host batch. What happens?
options: The play continues because one failure is less than half the batch
The play aborts because 1 / 3 is about 33.3%, which is greater than 33
The play continues because failure percentage must be greater than 100
Ansible automatically retries the complete inventory
questions.explanation: max_fail_percentage is evaluated per serial batch and aborts when the percentage is strictly greater than the threshold. One of three is approximately 33.3%.

questions.question: What does a successful ansible-playbook --check run prove?
options: Every task will behave identically during a real run
The managed hosts can never drift afterward
Supporting modules predicted no rejected change for that simulated path, but a real disposable-environment test is still needed
All secret values are safe to print with --diff
questions.explanation: Check mode is a simulation. Module support varies, registered results can differ, and external side effects or integrations still need realistic testing.

questions.question: A rolling task finishes on a host and the process is running, but the application cannot reach its database. Which gate should decide whether the host returns to service?
options: A user-visible readiness check that includes the dependency contract required to serve traffic
The package installation result alone
The controller's available memory
The alphabetical position of the host in inventory
questions.explanation: The rollout should re-enable traffic only after an application-level readiness check proves the host can serve its required request path.
